merger_description:
Novonesis A/S (**Novonesis**) proposes to indirectly acquire 100% of the outstanding issued and to be issued share capital of Microbiogen Pty Ltd (**Microbiogen**) through its wholly owned subsidiary, Novozymes Australia Pty Ltd (**Novozymes**) (the **Acquisition**).

Novonesis is a global biotechnology company headquartered in Denmark. Novonesis manufactures and supplies enzymes and microorganisms for industrial applications across multiple sectors. In Australia, it operates through its wholly owned subsidiary Novozymes, which operates as the regional sales, distribution and technical support arm of Novonesis in Australia and New Zealand.

Novonesis is majority owned and controlled by Novo Holdings A/S, which is in turn wholly owned by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, an independent enterprise foundation based in Hellerup, Denmark.

Microbiogen is a biotechnology company based in Sydney, Australia. Microbiogen is active in the research and development of yeast strains for industrial applications across a range of sectors, including biofuels, baking, food, animal feed, beverages and biochemicals.

Novonesis currently holds an existing minority shareholding in Microbiogen and via the Acquisition proposes to indirectly acquire the outstanding share capital in Microbiogen that is not already owned by Novonesis.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There is no horizontal overlap between the Parties.
• Novonesis would not have the ability and incentive to foreclose
rivals’ access to yeast strain research and development services
and associated intellectual property post-Acquisition given the
alternative providers of these services.
